subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should this trusted inbound-decoration state become a durable top-level message contract, or should it live in the existing OpenClaw-owned message metadata boundary before consumers are updated?
rationale: The PR changes persisted/runtime message shape and exports a shared resolver across core and memory-host surfaces; the correct permanent ownership boundary is a maintainer product and compatibility decision, not a mechanical review choice.

options.title: Use owner-scoped metadata
options.body: Move the trusted decoration state into the established OpenClaw-owned metadata boundary, then update the shared resolver and consumers to read only that canonical carrier.

options.title: Approve top-level fields explicitly
options.body: Accept `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` as a durable generic message contract, with compatibility documentation and focused contract coverage.

options.title: Narrow the PR
options.body: Limit this branch to correcting one affected reader while a separate maintainer-owned design establishes the persistent contract.

recommendation.title: Use owner-scoped metadata
recommendation.body: Move the trusted decoration state into the established OpenClaw-owned metadata boundary, then update the shared resolver and consumers to read only that canonical carrier.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main feature ownership could not be established safely without the required history inspection.
